descricao_original: The pancreas is both an exocrine and an endocrine gland. The endocrine pancreas consists of accumulations of pale-staining cells called islets of Langerhans, which are surrounded by pancreatic acini. The islet is composed of different populations of cells that secrete insulin, glucagon, somatostatin or pancreatic polypeptide. These cell types are difficult to distinguish by conventional hematoxylin and eosin staining. Islets differentiate from the developing exocrine duct system and constitute 1-2% of the pancreas volume. 400x
creditos_identificados: Image source: Image taken of a slide in the University of Mississippi collection.
